title: Show the useful result before the tour
trigger: A product video spends its opening on menus and setup before revealing why the software matters.
action: Start the demonstration with the actual finished output or solved task, then show the few steps that produced it. Keep an obvious way to inspect the underlying workflow so the opening result is an invitation to understand rather than a misleading shortcut.
mechanism: An early concrete payoff may give viewers a reason to invest attention in the explanation.
guardrail: Use genuine current output; label edits and do not conceal essential work or required paid features.
measure: Demo-to-paid activation; result-expectation mismatch.

title: Offer one guided interactive task
trigger: A complex product requires a full account and setup before a prospect can experience any meaningful interaction.
action: Create a clearly labeled sample environment that guides visitors through one representative task using safe data. End with the useful result and an explanation of how to perform the same task in a real account, without pretending the sample is live work.
mechanism: A small successful interaction may reduce uncertainty about ability and value.
guardrail: Prevent production side effects; distinguish simulated behavior from actual product capability and preserve access to pricing.
measure: Qualified paid activation after sample completion; sample-to-product mismatch.

title: Let visitors try an appropriate input
trigger: Generic samples fail to answer whether the product works on a prospect's own type of material.
action: Where the product and data policy support it, let visitors submit a small appropriate input for a bounded preview. Explain handling, limits and deletion before submission, and show the result without silently creating a paid commitment.
mechanism: Personal relevance may make an otherwise abstract capability easier to evaluate.
guardrail: Do not invite confidential data into an unsuitable public demo; enforce actual limits and obtain approval for any changed processing policy.
measure: Qualified paid conversion; data-handling complaints and preview costs.

title: Provide a realistic sample dataset
trigger: A demo opens with empty screens and asks visitors to invent data before anything useful happens.
action: Load an optional representative sample dataset with enough variation to demonstrate the core task. Label it as sample data and provide a clear reset, letting the prospect see the behavior before deciding whether to bring their own inputs.
mechanism: Reducing preparation effort may help visitors reach a meaningful evaluation faster.
guardrail: Use licensed non-sensitive examples; do not make a clean sample imply that all customer data requires no preparation.
measure: Sample task completion and paid activation; input-quality surprises.

title: Show input and output together
trigger: A polished result appears without revealing what information the product needed to create it.
action: Place a representative input beside its actual output and annotate the important transformation. Let the buyer inspect both at a readable scale, including any user corrections needed, so they can evaluate whether the change is useful.
mechanism: A visible transformation may make the mechanism and value easier to understand.
guardrail: Use the same example on both sides and current behavior; do not cherry-pick away material failure or manual work.
measure: Qualified purchases; input/output misunderstanding.

title: Let evaluators jump to their question
trigger: A long demonstration forces every viewer through the same sequence even when they need one specific answer.
action: Add meaningful chapters or indexed sections for core tasks, integrations, review controls and final outputs. Keep a short recommended path, while allowing a buyer to reach the part that addresses their current uncertainty directly.
mechanism: Control over attention may reduce the effort of evaluating a complex product.
guardrail: Verify chapter labels and timestamps; do not hide material limitations only in rarely visited sections.
measure: Qualified demo progression and paid conversion; unanswered objections.

title: State the real demonstration duration
trigger: Visitors cannot judge the time commitment of a video or interactive preview and postpone starting it.
action: Show the actual duration or estimated task length beside the preview, with a concise description of what they will learn. Provide a shorter overview only when it remains an accurate representation of the workflow.
mechanism: A bounded attention commitment may make starting feel easier.
guardrail: Measure or accurately label duration; preserve user control and avoid autoplay audio or an unskippable sales sequence.
measure: Demo starts leading to paid activation; premature exits.

title: Reveal the user's decisions during automation
trigger: An automated-looking demo hides where the user supplies information, reviews output or approves actions.
action: Mark the actual decision points in the demonstration and show one meaningful user choice changing the outcome. Explain what the software handles afterward, so the buyer understands both assistance and responsibility.
mechanism: Visible control may reduce uncertainty about adopting an automated workflow.
guardrail: Do not add fictional approval steps or imply the user can edit outputs when the product cannot support it.
measure: Qualified paid activation; control-related dissatisfaction.

title: Represent waiting time honestly
trigger: A demonstration jumps instantly from input to output while actual processing requires noticeable time.
action: Show the real waiting state or clearly disclose a sped-up segment and provide a measured typical range when available. Explain whether the buyer can continue other work or receives a notification while the process completes.
mechanism: Accurate timing may protect trust while making the workflow easier to plan.
guardrail: Do not invent performance figures; distinguish demo hardware, workload and network conditions from customer outcomes.
measure: Paid activation; latency-related refunds and complaints.

title: Demonstrate a recoverable failure
trigger: The product is useful but buyers worry that a mistake or failed input will leave them stuck.
action: Include a short example of an ordinary validation error or incomplete result and the real recovery path. Show that useful work is preserved when supported, then complete the task so the demonstration answers the practical consequence of failure.
mechanism: A visible recovery path may reduce perceived risk of trying the product.
guardrail: Use an actual supported recovery behavior; do not stage protection against failures the product cannot handle.
measure: Qualified purchases; failed first-task abandonment.

title: Annotate the decisive part of an output
trigger: Product screenshots contain useful evidence, but viewers do not know which detail demonstrates the benefit.
action: Add a few concise annotations to the actual interface or output identifying the decisive change, such as the assigned owner or traceable source. Keep the unannotated view available when needed and avoid covering essential context.
mechanism: Directed attention may help buyers notice the part that makes the result valuable.
guardrail: Do not annotate nonexistent features or imply selected examples are universal outcomes; keep annotations readable and accessible.
measure: Output comprehension and paid activation; mistaken feature expectations.

title: Let prospects keep a useful sample
trigger: An evaluation produces a helpful result, but the visitor cannot inspect it outside the demo or use it later.
action: Offer an export of the permitted sample output in a format the real product supports. Identify any demo watermark or limitation before starting, and let the retained artifact serve as a concrete reference during the purchase decision.
mechanism: A useful take-away may strengthen understanding and a sense of legitimate value received.
guardrail: Do not hold a promised free sample hostage behind an undisclosed payment; protect licensed and personal data.
measure: Qualified purchases from sample users; export mismatch and abuse cost.

title: Allow meaningful edits to the preview
trigger: A generated-output demo feels like a static advertisement because visitors cannot influence the result.
action: Expose one real control that materially changes the preview, such as the requested format, review setting or relevant input. Show the resulting difference and explain which controls exist in the product rather than adding decorative sliders.
mechanism: Active involvement may help prospects understand the product's controllability and personal fit.
guardrail: Use genuine supported behavior; do not imply customization that requires a different plan without stating it.
measure: Interactive-demo paid conversion; customization disappointment.

title: Make the API example runnable safely
trigger: Developers see attractive code snippets but cannot tell whether an integration produces the promised response.
action: Provide a small current example using a sandbox or safe sample credentials, with the expected response and error handling. Explain where a real key would go and what the production prerequisites are, without executing paid or destructive requests.
mechanism: Reproducible action may reduce integration uncertainty and demonstrate practical usefulness.
guardrail: Never expose secrets or run production side effects; verify current API syntax and sample licensing.
measure: Qualified developer purchases; integration failures and accidental costs.

title: Offer a clearly labeled dry run
trigger: A product changes important external systems, so prospects hesitate to evaluate its behavior.
action: Where an existing safe mode exists, demonstrate what would change without applying it. Present the proposed actions and limitations clearly, letting the visitor inspect the result before separately choosing whether to use the real workflow.
mechanism: A reversible evaluation may reduce perceived commitment and fear of accidental action.
guardrail: Verify that the dry run has no hidden side effects; adding a new execution mode requires appropriate implementation and validation.
measure: Qualified paid adoption; unintended-action incidents.

title: Compare complete workflows on one task
trigger: The product's advantage depends on fewer handoffs, but the demonstration only shows its own polished screen.
action: Show the actual end-to-end task using the current alternative and the product with the same inputs and completion criterion. Include setup and review that matter, and allow the buyer to inspect each sequence rather than relying on an unexplained speed claim.
mechanism: A fair process comparison may make an operational advantage tangible.
guardrail: Do not manipulate workloads or timing; label conditions and avoid financial savings claims unsupported by the comparison.
measure: Qualified paid conversion; workflow comparison disputes.

title: Identify the plan used in demonstrations
trigger: A compelling demo showcases an advanced capability that buyers later discover is absent from the plan they selected.
action: Label the demonstrated plan and any required add-on beside the relevant capability, and link to its actual offer. Where useful, include a basic-plan example so visitors can evaluate an attainable version without guessing feature availability.
mechanism: Clear feature-to-offer mapping may reduce evaluation confusion and purchase regret.
guardrail: Use the canonical entitlement catalog; do not steer buyers through a demo of unavailable functionality.
measure: Plan-fit purchases; missing-feature refunds.

title: Expose the source behind generated answers
trigger: An AI result looks useful, but prospects cannot tell whether it is grounded in their supplied material.
action: Demonstrate the actual source-inspection or provenance feature by connecting a result to the input passage or record that supports it. Show how a user checks the reference and handle unsupported statements as the product genuinely does.
mechanism: Inspectable grounding may make evaluation more confident for buyers who must verify outputs.
guardrail: Only demonstrate provenance the product supplies; citations are not a guarantee of correctness and must not be fabricated.
measure: Qualified paid activation; unsupported-output incidents.

title: Provide the uncut workflow behind highlights
trigger: A short marketing clip leaves careful prospects unsure which steps were omitted or simplified.
action: Link the highlights to a complete representative task recording or walkthrough that includes essential setup, waiting and review. Keep the short version useful, while allowing a buyer to inspect the actual effort before committing.
mechanism: Optional depth may make a concise demonstration credible without burdening every visitor.
guardrail: Use current behavior and label edits, simulated data and exceptional conditions; do not reveal private customer content.
measure: Qualified purchases after deeper evaluation; effort surprises.

title: Make demo results safely shareable
trigger: A prospect needs another person's opinion but cannot share what they evaluated without recreating the task.
action: Provide a user-controlled shareable sample or export containing the result, assumptions and product context. Make access permissions explicit and preserve a stable reference so another evaluator can understand the same evidence independently.
mechanism: Shared concrete evidence may help a buying group discuss value with less explanation effort.
guardrail: Default private inputs to private access; do not auto-message colleagues or turn a sample link into public customer data.
measure: Shared-evaluation paid conversion; access-control incidents.
